title: Reference map
description: A game's data folder described for the editor without touching its schemas: which list items take their label from which field, and which fields hold ids of items in another list, so the table and inspector can show a readable name and follow the link. It's metadata about paths, never a copy of the game's records. General: any game can write one.

game.description: Whose data this describes, for people reading it.

labels.description: List items whose readable name is one of their fields, where the editor's own guess (name, id, title) finds none.

references.description: Fields whose value is the id of an item somewhere else.

place.description: A JSON Pointer in which * stands for any list index or any key at that step, such as /factories/*/methods/*/inputs/*/of.

file.description: A data file's name within the folder.

list.description: The list whose items are labelled.

field.description: The string field that names each item. Give this or template, not both.

template.description: A label made from several fields: each {field} is replaced by that field's value ("{of} x{count}"). A label whose fields are all missing falls back to the editor's own guess.

at.description: Where the id is held. If the place is a list of strings, each one is an id.

keys.description: True when the ids are the keys of the object at this place, not its values.

list.description: The list (or keyed object) the ids name items of.

key.description: The field holding each item's id; "$key" when the items are an object's keys; "$value" when the list holds plain values (strings or numbers) that are the ids themselves.

where.description: Conditions every candidate target must meet, all of them : a field of the candidate equal to a value near the source, or a field the candidate lacks. A source value that isn't there makes the whole lookup NeedsScope; a candidate whose field isn't there doesn't count.

at.description: A Relative JSON Pointer from the candidate item, such as "0/owner".

equalsSource.description: A Relative JSON Pointer from the source value, such as "2#" (the key two levels up).

absent.description: A field the candidate object must not have.

also.description: Further places the same id may name, tried in order (a ware or a ware family, say). An id found in more than one is ambiguous and isn't followed.

scope.description: When the target is local, the part of the source place that narrows it, in words ("the same sector"). The adapter handles scoped references; the map only says so.

sentinels.description: Values that are deliberately not ids ("none", "pirate"), so they're never reported as missing.

evidence.description: Where the game says so: a schema line or validator rule, relative to the game's repository.

checked.description: What resolving every value against the real data found when the map was written.

parts.description: An id made of parts ("meridian/terran", "gene:choice"): split at the separator, each part resolved against its own target, in order; null for a part that isn't an id. When given, it replaces target for resolving; target stays as the place's main target, for people reading the map.

narrow.description: Narrows the target to the items inside one container, named by a value near the source: by is a Relative JSON Pointer from the source value ("1/sector": the sibling field sector; "2#": the key two levels up), and that value is looked up in the container list by key. Only target places inside that container count. It makes a scope machine-readable; scope stays for people.
